claim_verdicts.evidence: "Commands that modify the filesystem create a new layer. The FROM statement starts out by creating a layer from the ubuntu:22.04 image. The LABEL command only modifies the image's metadata, and doesn't produce a new layer." "Each layer is only a set of differences from the layer before it." Live `docker history donhang-lab:stage-0`: EXPOSE, ENV, LABEL, ARG, VOLUME rows all 0B; RUN/COPY/ADD rows non-zero. Lesson wording ("add no files") is safe.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/engine/storage/drivers/_index.md (lines 46-72); docker history on the running lab

claim_verdicts.evidence: "Each subsequent instruction is compared against the cached layers. If no cached layer matches the instruction exactly, the cache is invalidated." "For the ADD and COPY instructions ... the builder calculates a cache checksum from file metadata" "just the command string itself is used to find a match." "Once the cache is invalidated, all subsequent Dockerfile commands generate new images and the cache isn't used."

git show stage-0:scripts/up.sh and stage-1:scripts/up.sh both contain `docker compose up -d --build --wait`. Reuse on later runs confirmed by `docker compose build lab`: `#5 [lab 2/2] RUN apk add ... #5 CACHED`, real 0m1.099s.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Plain (non-TTY) output, as captured: `#5 [lab 2/2] RUN apk add --no-cache ...` then `#5 CACHED`. In an interactive terminal the default TTY progress puts CACHED first on one line, as in the docs: " => CACHED [base 1/2] FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu". The lesson tells the learner to run it "in a terminal on your own machine", so they will most likely see `=> CACHED [lab 2/2] RUN apk add ...`.
claim_verdicts.source: docker compose build lab (live, non-TTY); refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/build/building/multi-stage.md line 178
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: 2 — the `[lab 2/2] RUN apk add ...` step is marked `CACHED` (in a terminal: `=> CACHED [lab 2/2] RUN apk add ...`), and the build finishes in a moment.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "The builder begins by checking if the base image is already cached. Each subsequent instruction is compared against the cached layers. If no cached layer matches the instruction exactly, the cache is invalidated." "Once the cache is invalidated, all subsequent Dockerfile commands generate new images". "Once a layer changes, then all downstream layers need to be rebuilt as well."

"If your build contains several layers and you want to ensure the build cache is reusable, order the instructions from less frequently changed to more frequently changed where possible." Lesson states the condition ("so a small change rebuilds only a little").
